items.stem: Under the NPV rule, a project should normally be accepted when its NPV is:

options.rationale: Correct: a positive NPV adds value and should be accepted.
A negative NPV destroys value and should be rejected.
Zero NPV is the breakeven, not a clear accept signal.

options.text: The largest in absolute size regardless of sign
options.rationale: Size does not override a negative sign.

items.explanation: Correct: a positive NPV adds value and should be accepted.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which two are weaknesses of the simple payback method? (Select TWO)

options.text: It ignores cash flows after the payback point
options.rationale: Correct: payback disregards later cash flows.

options.text: It ignores the time value of money
options.rationale: Correct: simple payback does not discount.

options.text: It requires a discount rate to compute
options.rationale: Simple payback needs no discount rate, which is part of the problem.

items.explanation: Correct: payback disregards later cash flows.

items.stem: A cost already incurred that cannot be recovered should be treated in a project appraisal as:

options.text: Irrelevant (a sunk cost) and excluded from the decision
options.rationale: Correct: sunk costs do not change with the decision.

options.text: A relevant cash outflow to include
options.rationale: Sunk costs are not relevant to the decision.
A past cost is not a future benefit.
It is unrelated to the discount rate.

items.explanation: Correct: sunk costs do not change with the decision.
